overview.historicalContext: Wantzel (1837) proved that a number is constructible by compass and straightedge iff it lies in a tower of quadratic extensions over ℚ, finally resolving the ancient Greek impossibility questions (angle trisection, cube duplication, circle squaring). Galois theory, developed by Galois (1832) and systematized in the 19th century, recharacterizes this: constructibility is equivalent to the Galois group of the minimal polynomial being a 2-group (a group of order 2^n). The equivalence of these two formulations — quadratic tower criterion ↔ Galois 2-group criterion — is a fundamental result connecting classical constructibility with modern algebraic structure theory. Remarkably, Galois was killed in a duel at age 20 in 1832 before his work was published; it took 14 years for Liouville to recognize its importance.
overview.problemStatement: Can the equivalence between the quadratic tower criterion and the Galois 2-group criterion for constructibility be proved using Mathlib's Galois correspondence?
overview.text: Formalizes the Tower ↔ Galois 2-group equivalence for constructibility with a proper inductive tower definition
overview.proofStrategy: Define QuadraticTower inductively (base: ⊥, step: extend by degree 2). For Tower → Galois: show the splitting field degree is a power of 2. For Galois → Tower: use index-2 subgroups (which exist in non-trivial 2-groups) and the Galois correspondence to peel off quadratic extensions.
keyInsights: The previous TowerCriterion = DegreeCriterion alias was mathematically incorrect — a proper inductive definition is needed
The hard direction (Galois → Tower) reduces to: every non-trivial 2-group has a subgroup of index 2
The main bottleneck for a full Lean proof is API glue between Polynomial.Gal and IntermediateField, not missing theory
Both IsPGroup.isSolvable and IsPGroup.to_subgroup are directly available from Mathlib

The inductive QuadraticTower definition is essential: the naive alias TowerCriterion = DegreeCriterion would conflate two different equivalences (tower structure vs degree condition), obscuring the structural reason why 2-groups and quadratic towers are equivalent

sections.title: Proper Quadratic Tower Definition
sections.summary: Inductive definition of QuadraticTower and ConstructibleViaTower, replacing the previous alias.
sections.mathContext: A quadratic tower is defined inductively: base case is ⊥ (= F), inductive step extends by a degree-2 extension. This captures the geometric notion of compass-and-straightedge construction steps.

sections.title: Tower → Degree 2^n
sections.summary: Proof that a quadratic tower of height n has total degree 2^n, and that tower constructibility implies the degree criterion.
sections.mathContext: By induction on the tower structure: the base has degree 2^0 = 1, and each step multiplies the degree by 2 via the tower law.

sections.title: 2-Group Structure Lemmas
sections.summary: Key structural facts about 2-groups: index-2 subgroups exist, order is 2^n, subgroups and solvability.
sections.mathContext: The existence of index-2 subgroups in non-trivial 2-groups is the key structural lemma. Combined with the Galois correspondence, it gives the 'next step' in building a quadratic tower from a 2-group.

sections.title: Galois Correspondence Connection
sections.summary: Statement of the core theorem: Galois 2-group → quadratic tower, with detailed proof sketch.
sections.mathContext: The proof iteratively extracts index-2 subgroups from the Galois group, using the Galois correspondence to convert each to a degree-2 field extension step.

sections.title: The Full Tower ↔ Galois Equivalence
sections.summary: Statement of the complete equivalence combining both directions.
sections.mathContext: This is the Wantzel-Galois characterization of constructibility: α is constructible ↔ Gal(minpoly ℚ α) is a 2-group.

sections.title: Feasibility Assessment for Mathlib
sections.summary: Detailed analysis of what Mathlib provides and what API glue is missing for a complete proof.
sections.mathContext: Identifies 4 specific gaps: Polynomial.Gal ↔ IntermediateField bridge, index-2 subgroup existence, index-degree relation, and iterative tower construction. Estimates ~500-800 lines of Lean 4.

conclusion.summary: The Tower ↔ Galois equivalence CAN be proved using Mathlib's Galois correspondence, but requires ~500-800 lines of API glue. The main bottleneck is connecting Polynomial.Gal to IntermediateField.fixingSubgroup, not missing mathematical theory.
conclusion.implications: A complete proof would be a valuable Mathlib contribution, bridging the gap between polynomial Galois groups and field extension Galois groups in the library.
openQuestions: Can the API glue between Polynomial.Gal and IntermediateField be contributed to Mathlib?
Can the index-2 subgroup lemma be proved purely from Mathlib's p-group theory?

mainTheorems.name: tower_iff_galois_two_group
mainTheorems.description: The full Tower ↔ Galois 2-group equivalence for constructibility
mainTheorems.leanType: (α : ℝ) → (hα : IsIntegral ℚ α) → ConstructibleViaTower α ↔ IsPGroup 2 (minpoly ℚ α).Gal

mainTheorems.name: quadratic_tower_degree
mainTheorems.description: A quadratic tower of height n has degree 2^n
mainTheorems.leanType: (K : IntermediateField ℚ ℝ) → (n : ℕ) → QuadraticTower ℚ ℝ K n → FiniteDimensional ℚ K ∧ Module.finrank ℚ K = 2 ^ n

mainTheorems.name: exists_index_two_subgroup
mainTheorems.description: Every non-trivial finite 2-group has a subgroup of index 2
mainTheorems.leanType: {G : Type*} → [Group G] → [Fintype G] → IsPGroup 2 G → Fintype.card G > 1 → ∃ H : Subgroup G, H.index = 2
